base_rationale: CAM is the recommended base for 1Sa17. CAM preserves the LONG/FULL form (58 verses, 884 tokens) including the complete David-introduction (17:12-31) and the post-duel Abner 'whose son is this youth' block (17:55-58); GG transmits only the SHORT LXX-type duel core (20 verses, compressed paraphrase) and omits ~38 verses' worth of narrative. CAM is thus the textually most complete and continuous witness for the chapter, with no illegible tokens and a low 9.62% scribal-uncertainty rate. The very low W-W agreement is the expected, honest signature of two distinct recensions, not a defect of either transcription.

verses.semantic_note: 1Sa17:1 -- Philistines gather their armies at Socoh of Judah, encamp between Socoh and Azekah at Ephes-dammim -- GG carries this (compressed) as GG v1.
1Sa17:2 -- Saul and the men of Israel gather and encamp by the valley of Elah, set the battle in array against the Philistines -- CAM-only plus (GG's short opening compresses this away).
1Sa17:3 -- Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, Israel on a mountain on the other, a valley between -- CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:4 -- a champion came out of the Philistine camp, Goliath of Gath, six cubits and a span -- GG carries the champion's defiance as GG v2.
1Sa17:5 -- he had a helmet of brass and was armed with a coat of mail -- CAM-only plus (GG's short form omits the armour description).
1Sa17:6 -- greaves of brass on his legs and a target of brass between his shoulders -- CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:7 -- the staff of his spear was like a weaver's beam; one bearing his shield went before him -- CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:8 -- he stood and cried to the armies of Israel: why are you come to set battle? choose a man -- CAM-only plus (GG compresses the challenge).
1Sa17:9 -- 'if he be able to fight me and kill me we will be your servants; if I prevail you shall serve us' -- CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:10 -- 'I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man that we may fight together' -- CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:11 -- Saul and all Israel heard the Philistine's words, were dismayed and greatly afraid -- CAM-only plus (GG folds the fear into GG v2).
1Sa17:12 -- David the son of Jesse the Ephrathite of Bethlehem-judah, who had eight sons -- David-introduction block; CAM-only plus, GG omits it.
1Sa17:13 -- the three eldest sons of Jesse (Eliab, Abinadab, Shammah) went with Saul to the battle -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:14 -- David was the youngest; the three eldest followed Saul -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:15 -- but David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:16 -- the Philistine drew near morning and evening forty days -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:17 -- Jesse said to David: take this parched corn and ten loaves to your brothers in the camp -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:18 -- carry ten cheeses to the captain of their thousand, see how your brothers fare, take their pledge -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:19 -- Saul and all Israel were in the valley of Elah fighting the Philistines -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:20 -- David rose early, left the sheep with a keeper, went as Jesse commanded and came to the trench as the host went to fight -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:21 -- Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:22 -- David left his carriage with the keeper, ran to the army and greeted his brothers -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:23 -- as he talked, the champion Goliath the Philistine came up and spoke the same defiance, and David heard -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:24 -- all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid -- David-introduction; CAM-only plus.
1Sa17:25 -- men of Israel: have you seen this man? the king will enrich the one who kills him and give his daughter -- GG carries this as GG v3.
1Sa17:26 -- David asks the men what is done for him who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach -- 'who is this uncircumcised?' -- GG carries this as GG v4.
1Sa17:27 -- the people answered him after the same manner: so shall it be done to the man who kills him -- CAM-only plus (GG compresses; GG v4 folds 25/26).
1Sa17:28 -- Eliab heard, was angry at David: why came down, with whom left the sheep, I know your pride -- GG carries this as GG v5.
1Sa17:29 -- David: 'what have I now done? is it not but a word?' -- GG folds this into GG v6 (anchored at CAM 30).
1Sa17:30 -- he turned from him to another and spoke as before; the people answered him again -- GG carries this as GG v6.
1Sa17:31 -- when David's words were heard they rehearsed them before Saul, and he sent for him -- CAM-only plus (GG v6 ends 'told before Saul').
1Sa17:32 -- David to Saul: let no man's heart fail; your servant will go and fight this Philistine -- GG folds this into GG v7 (anchored at CAM 33).
1Sa17:33 -- Saul to David: you cannot go against him, you are a youth, he a man of war from his youth -- GG carries this as GG v7.
1Sa17:34 -- David: your servant kept his father's sheep; when a lion or bear took a lamb I went after it -- GG carries this as GG v8.
1Sa17:35 -- 'I caught it by the throat, smote and slew it' -- GG folds this into GG v8 (anchored at CAM 34).
1Sa17:36 -- 'this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God' -- GG carries this as GG v9.
1Sa17:37 -- David: Yahweh who saved me from lion and bear will save me from this Philistine; Saul: go, Yahweh be with you -- GG carries this as GG v10.
1Sa17:38 -- Saul armed David with his armour, a brass helmet, a coat of mail -- GG carries this as GG v11.
1Sa17:39 -- David girded the sword, assayed to go, could not (not proved it) and put it off -- GG folds this into GG v11/v12 (anchored at CAM 38/40).
1Sa17:40 -- David took his staff, chose smooth stones from the brook into his scrip, sling in hand, drew near the Philistine -- GG carries this as GG v12.
1Sa17:41 -- the Philistine came on and drew near David, his shield-bearer before him -- CAM-only plus (GG compresses the approach).
1Sa17:42 -- the Philistine looked about, saw David and disdained him, a ruddy fair youth -- GG carries this as GG v13.
1Sa17:43 -- the Philistine: 'am I a dog that you come with staves?' and cursed David by his gods -- GG folds this into GG v13/v14 (anchored CAM 42/44).
1Sa17:44 -- the Philistine: 'come to me and I will give your flesh to the birds and beasts' -- GG carries this as GG v14.
1Sa17:45 -- David: you come with sword and spear, I come in the name of Yahweh of hosts whom you have defied -- GG carries this as GG v15.
1Sa17:46 -- 'today Yahweh will deliver you into my hand, I will smite you and take your head and give the carcases to the birds and beasts' -- GG folds this into GG v15/v16 (anchored at CAM 45/47).
1Sa17:47 -- 'and all this assembly shall know Yahweh saves not with sword and spear; the battle is Yahweh's, he will give you into our hand' -- GG carries this as GG v16.
1Sa17:48 -- the Philistine arose and drew near; David hasted and ran toward the army to meet him -- GG folds this into GG v17 (anchored at CAM 49).
1Sa17:49 -- David put his hand in his bag, took a stone, slung it, smote the Philistine in the forehead; he fell on his face -- GG carries this as GG v17.
1Sa17:50 -- so David prevailed with a sling and a stone; there was no sword in David's hand -- GG folds this into GG v18 (anchored at CAM 51).

1Sa17:51 -- David ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword and slew him and cut off his head; the Philistines saw their champion dead and fled -- GG carries this as GG v18 (with the dittographic ወርጸ ዳዊት head).
1Sa17:52 -- the men of Israel and Judah arose, shouted, pursued the Philistines to Gath and Ekron; the slain fell by the way -- GG carries this as GG v19.
1Sa17:53 -- the children of Israel returned from chasing the Philistines and spoiled their tents -- GG folds this into GG v19 (anchored at CAM 52).
1Sa17:54 -- David took the head of the Philistine to Jerusalem and put his armour in his tent -- GG carries this as GG v20 (= 1Sa 17:54, GG's last verse).
1Sa17:55 -- Saul, seeing David go out, said to Abner: whose son is this youth? Abner: as your soul lives I cannot tell -- Abner block; CAM-only plus, GG omits 55-58 (the LXX-short recension).
1Sa17:56 -- the king: enquire whose son the stripling is -- Abner block; CAM-only plus, absent in GG.
1Sa17:57 -- when David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him before Saul with the head in his hand -- Abner block; CAM-only plus.

1Sa17:58 -- Saul: whose son are you, young man? David: I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite -- Abner block; CAM-only plus; CAM ch.17 ends here, ch.18 (Jonathan's soul knit to David's) follows.

metrics.lacuna_counts_note: Both evidence files contain 0 ⟦illegible⟧ tokens (GG 0, CAM 0), so there are 0 lacuna-* rows and lacuna_counts is {gg:0,cam:0,both:0}. ALIGNMENT SCHEME: CAM is the verse spine (one contiguous row per CAM verse v=1..58, CAM being the fuller witness and recommended base); GG's 20 verses are mapped onto CAM verses by NARRATIVE CONTENT (never positional v==v) using the 1sa.py skeleton + the David-&-Goliath narrative. EXTENT DIVERGENCE: this is the single most famous LXX-vs-MT recensional split in Samuel -- GG is the SHORT LXX-type form (20 vv, duel core only) and CAM is the LONG/FULL form (58 vv); the Kenyon witness-note at skeleton 1Sa17:12 independently states the best LXX MSS omit exactly 17:12-31,41,50,55-58, matching GG. The ~38 CAM verses with no GG counterpart (David-introduction 12-24, parts of 27/29/31/32/35/39/41/43/46/48/50/53, and the Abner block 55-58) are genuine recensional textual MINUS: every such row is a one-sided {gg:'',cam:<tok>,class:disagree} and IS counted in the aligned denominator. Recensional absence is NOT lacuna -- lacuna is physical illegibility only, of which there is none.

definitions.strict: exact literal token-string identity / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs
definitions.skeleton: diacritic/order-folded + near-homograph-folded token equality (class==agree) / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs, full aligned denominator
definitions.both_confident: skeleton-equal / aligned pairs where neither witness flagged that token uncertain or illegible (gap/insertion cells and lacuna rows also excluded from this denominator)
